result:
Both bugs are fixed and the full suite passes (6 passed). Summary:

**`lrucache/cache.py`** had two LRU-correctness bugs:

1. **`get` never refreshed recency** — it returned the value without `move_to_end`, so a read key stayed marked least-recently-used and got evicted on the next `put`. Fixed by adding `self._data.move_to_end(key)` before returning.

2. **`put` evicted on in-place updates** — the eviction guard was `len(self._data) >= self.capacity`, which triggered even when updating an existing key, wrongly popping the LRU entry at full capacity. Fixed by guarding with `key not in self._data and ...`.

I also wrote `SOLUTION.md` explaining both root causes. The tests under `tests/` were left untouched, and no commits were made.
